title: 10th Anniversary, Ceremony, and The Adventures of the Fluffy Hero
text: “Huh?”

I’d come to the town library to read. I’m Naofumi Iwatani, a sophomore in college. I’m aware that I’m a bit more of an otaku than most people. Ever since I discovered various video games, anime, and otaku culture, I’ve been devoting myself to them more seriously than to my studies. I was browsing the section dedicated to classic fantasy. After all, the history of fantasy is as old as human history itself. Even the Bible, when you get right down to it, is a fantasy novel.
“The Book of the Four Holy Weapons?”

Just as I was reading that book, my consciousness began to drift away. I never would have dreamed that this would send me to another world, or that the events that followed would lead to such an incredible experience.
“The Spear Hero, the Source of All Power, commands: Interpret the universe once more, and transform the forms of those beings.”
“Al-Fairy-Morph!”
The moment I regained consciousness, a loud “Boom!” echoed through the air, and thick smoke billowed everywhere.
“Guh! Guh!”

I couldn’t help but choke and gasp for air. If I’d woken up to that, I’d have thought, “What’s going on? Is there a fire or something?” So, wondering what was happening, I looked around and saw that some kind of cloth was wrapped around my body. I tried to tear it off in a hurry, but it didn’t work, so I ended up wriggling my way out.
“Guh… Guh-guh.”
“What on earth is this?”
“Seriously… what’s going on…”

And then, just as the smoke began to clear… all around me were… a rabbit, a dog, and a squirrel? Well, they were creatures that looked like those family-friendly dolls aimed at little girls. They were all wearing something that looked like Santa hats. The rabbit was holding a spear, and the dog—which looked like a Siberian Husky with a different coat pattern—was holding a sword. The squirrel had a bow… the same weapons as the heroes in the *Book of the Four Holy Weapons* I’d been reading? These mysterious doll-like—or rather, stuffed animal-like—creatures were all staring at one another… The way they were standing on two legs looked really fancy. But given the situation, could this be what they call a “summoning to another world”?　Or maybe some mysterious event happened while I was asleep? Looking around, there are stone walls and a magic circle on the ground that looks like it was drawn with fluorescent paint—based on the circumstances alone, it does seem like a summoning to another world… Is this a dream? I thought about pinching my cheek to check, but my hand… isn’t the one I’m used to—it’s something else… what is it? It’s too stiff to be a wing; it looks more like a flipper, and at the end of my line of sight, there’s something that looks like a beak. …Could it be that I, like this rabbit, dog, and squirrel, have taken on some other form? There’s a mysterious shield attached to my arm. Could it be that I’ve been reincarnated as a monster in some “reincarnation in another world” scenario? Like, I was summoned in the form of a monster or something like that.
“What on earth is this…”

Just as I was wondering what was going on, the dog holding a sword asked the man in the robe. Oh, our height… it’s shrunk drastically. Assuming they’re human, they’re so small that we have to look up at them.
“Whoa…”

I guess he’s going to explain the situation now? Well… I’m not entirely sure, but I’m starting to feel a sense of camaraderie with this rabbit, dog, and squirrel, and given the circumstances, I figure the summoner will explain something.
“Everyone! The summoning failed! Kill these things!”
A sudden “kill them” declaration!? Just as I thought that, the rabbit holding a spear raised it and thrust it with all his might.
“Guh—”
With just that single strike, the man in the robe was impaled, slammed into the wall, and stopped moving.
“Haaaaaa!”
“Dieeeee! You failed summons!”
“I can’t possibly recognize you as heroes!”
“Let’s settle this right here and now!”
With that, everyone in the room charged at us all at once. Their voices, filled with murderous intent, sent a chill right through my spine.
“Haaaa!”
The next to move after the rabbit was the dog wielding a sword. He slashed with his sword on the spot and rushed over to me and the squirrel.
“We’ve got to get out of here fast!”
“That’s right. These guys tried to kill us out of the blue. If we don’t run, we’ll get killed!”
“Uh, yeah… y-yeah, you’re right.”
“O-okay.”
Still struggling to process the situation, the Squirrel and I snapped back to our senses at the Rabbit and Dog’s words and steadied ourselves, having nearly lost our balance.
“Let’s go! Full speed ahead!”
“‘““Whaaaaaa!?””’”

When the rabbit guy swung his spear, a tornado erupted, sweeping away the people inside the room. What on earth was that attack? I mean, given the situation, it might be something like a summoning to another world or something. He’s gotten a lot shorter, after all. Maybe he’s already able to use some kind of mysterious power.
“Let’s get out of here fast!”
“If you want to die, we’ll leave you behind, right?”
The rabbit and the dog looked at me and the squirrel and asked.
“I’m not leaving you behind.”
“Hmph.”
The rabbit and the dog glared at each other over their disagreement, but the dog didn’t seem intent on causing a rift among the group and didn’t appear willing to argue any further.
“I’ll go ahead. Oto—everyone, follow me.”
“Do you know the way?”
“These ears of mine can pick up sounds. I don’t even need to look to know where things are.”
As he says this, he pounds his chest with his hand in a way that makes him seem incredibly reliable—though he does look rather fancy. …Except for the fact that he’s covered in blood, that is.
“Well then, let’s go all out! Motoyasu JUMP!”
With a “Bang!” the Rabbit—is his name Motoyasu, by any chance?—kicked the door open…　He looked around and beckoned to us.
“What the—!?”
“T-the summoning failed… I’ll take care of those guys—”
Just as he stepped out of the room, the guy who’d been lying on the floor shouted at a knight-like figure in armor. Immediately afterward, the knight-like figure blew a whistle.
“Emergency! Emergency! A Beastman has infiltrated the premises! Hurry and eliminate—”
Thud! The rabbit thrust his spear into the knight’s stomach. That spear… isn’t it stretching out a bit?
“You’re being noisy. Just lie there quietly.”
The knight glanced back and forth between his stomach and the spear.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
He let out a terrifying scream.
“Huh!?”
“Whoa…”
The rabbit and I let out small screams, while the dog furrowed his brow. Clang! Clang! The sound of bells echoing through the arena signaled an emergency.
“That was a mistake. This guy screams, doesn’t he?”

With a thud, the rabbit hurled the screaming knight against the wall to silence him. What on earth is he? Is he used to fighting? The dog guy also seems calm, as if he’s been through this before. I can hear the sound of a large crowd of people rushing toward us—thud, thud, thud. At this rate, the soldiers stationed here are going to gather around us. Where on earth can we run…?
“Let’s go.”
The rabbit guy points the way, so we follow his lead and start running.
“Hey, you. If you don’t run faster, we’ll get caught.”
The squirrel turned around to warn me.
“Even so, you should’ve said that after seeing what I look like!”
“Well… you are a penguin, after all. You’ve got the weakest legs of the bunch here… You’d be at a disadvantage on land.”
Could you stop feeling sorry for me? I mean… so I really am a penguin after all. I just realized it while looking at my hands, belly, and legs.
“It’s fine!”
The rabbit turned around and opened a window in the hallway.
“What are you planning to do? Are you actually going to climb out of there?”

I scrambled up the wall and looked outside… and there spread before me a scene that looked exactly like the kind of townscape you’d expect in medieval Europe. Normally, this would be the kind of situation you’d think was like a dream, but since I’d just been chased while being hurled death threats, it wasn’t exactly a moment to be moved by.
“Exactly so!”

The rabbit grabbed my arm—I’d been struggling to climb up and had somehow managed to get my face up to the window—and pulled me up. Then, still holding my arm, he guided me toward the window. But beyond the window wasn’t a place high enough to jump down from. There was no ledge or anything to step onto; it was just the window itself. Just because I was in the form of a small animal didn’t mean I could go places a human couldn’t. If I jumped out like that, I’d undoubtedly fall to my death.
“No, you’ll die! If you jump out from there!”
“What’s that supposed to mean? I—are you climbing walls or something? A squirrel… could do that, couldn’t they?”
Hmm… just as the squirrel was getting annoyed by the rabbit’s provocation, the dog started looking around restlessly.
“I guess my only option is to run away from here… but maybe I have no choice but to break through head-on.”
The sound of footsteps came rustling from both sides of the hallway.
“Just—”
“Whoa! Don’t grab my tail! Let go!”
“Ouch! Please don’t grab my cheek!”
The rabbit was grabbing the dog and squirrel by their tails and cheeks and pulling them.
“Oto—you’re going to let me catch you, right?”
“Ah… yeah.”

He seemed so confident—did he have some kind of plan? I signaled him out of the corner of my eye, as if asking the rabbit to wrap its arms around my neck, so I let myself be caught, even though my body wasn’t moving very well.
“Alright, here we go!”
With a “hop!” the rabbit, carrying me, the dog, and the squirrel, leaped out the window.
“Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Ooooooooooooooooh!”
“Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
As we each let out a scream and looked back, we realized we’d leaped out of a huge castle. Just as I thought the grassy courtyard was getting closer…
“Here we go!”

With a “Pyon!”—I don’t know what he used as a foothold—the rabbit jumped again, or rather, defied the laws of physics and dropped into the castle courtyard. It was a move that looked just like that plumber’s hip drop, the kind that negates damage from falling from a great height.
“Just hang in there a bit.”
“Eh, wait a sec—”

Just as I thought the rabbit had stopped grabbing the squirrel’s cheek, it clamped the squirrel’s head between its feet and spun a spear at high speed with one hand. Then, wobble-wobble, just like a helicopter, we slowly… managed to land. The dog and the squirrel landed with a thud and rolled, while I just planted my feet firmly on the ground.
“Ow, ow, ow…”
“I thought I was going to die! Were you trying to kill us?!”
Well… I couldn’t help but feel sorry for the squirrel, whose head was pinned between the rabbit’s feet while in midair.
“We haven’t escaped yet.”
“R-right! Let’s hurry and get out of here!”
“This way!”
And so, we continued down the path leading underground from what looked like a garden… and somehow managed to escape.
“Did you see them?”
“Nope… Let’s move on!”
Hiding behind cover in the basement, we lay low until the soldiers who had come searching passed by… and finally managed to catch our breath.
“It looks like… we managed to shake off our pursuers.”
“Yeah. Though there’s still a chance they’ll find us soon…”
Inu and Risu, having caught their breath, let out a small sigh.
“Sigh… Please let me rest just a little. It’s just… we’ve been on the move nonstop, and I’m a bit…”
“I feel the same way. We’re still inside the castle, right? We’ve got to find a way to escape outside.”
Hiding in the shadows, we caught our breath and looked at each other.
“Are you okay?”

Rabbit, whose breathing remained steady, spoke to me with a worried look. Is he… the most reliable one here? He’s the most battle-hardened, and while his escape routes are outlandish, he’s managed to secure a way out just like this.
“Um… thanks. Rabbit…”
“My name is Motoyasu Kitamura, you know.”
“O-oh, really? Nice to meet you, Motoyasu. I’m Naofumi Iwatani.”
So the rabbit’s name is Motoyasu Kitamura, apparently. He gives off a “Rabbit Pyonta” vibe, but I guess he does have a name after all.
“Got it. Naofumi…-kun. You look a lot like my father, so is it okay if I call you ‘Father’?”
“Wait, why out of the blue!?”

How on earth did Motoyasu the rabbit end up calling me ‘Father’? I mean, he gave a reason, but isn’t that a bit much to just go along with? Or is it that this rabbit guy—assuming this is an “summoned to another world” scenario—was a rabbit even before he was summoned? Like, he was a rabbit from the Kitamura family named Motoyasu, and that’s how he got summoned or something. I could understand it if the logic was that he thinks of his owner as “Father,” but accepting being called “Father” in a situation where we can actually talk…
“Is that okay?”
Don’t tilt your little head with that ‘kyurun’ sound and beg me like that… It’s hard to say no.
“Um…”
I’ll try to change the subject. Motoyasu… since he’s a rabbit, I’ll add ‘-kun’ to his name to make it sound more natural. I turn to the squirrel guy for help.

“…Given the situation, I guess we should introduce ourselves. Otherwise, we’ll end up calling each other by what we look like. My name is Itsuki Kawasumi—believe it or not, I used to be human. I’m a high school sophomore, 17 years old.”
“And you?” With that look on his face, the squirrel, Itsuki Kawasumi, asks the dog his name.
“I’m Ren Amaki. I’m a high school freshman, 16 years old. I’m human, of course. I just woke up looking like this.”
“So, based on the introductions earlier, you’re Naofumi-san and that’s Motoyasu-san, right? And you’re human?”
“Of course I am. What did you think I was?”
Wait… you were about to call me ‘Father,’ weren’t you? Even though there was that suspicion that a rabbit had been summoned to another world.
“Ah, so you named the penguin ‘Father’ and were raising it. That sounds like something out of a manga.”
Ah… I see. Come to think of it, if that’s the case… could it actually be possible?
“That’s not it. A Father is a Father. He’s definitely human.”
“No, that’s even more of a mystery.”
Seriously, why did you call me ‘Father’?
“Then let’s just say our voices sound alike.”
Ah, I can tell just by looking at Itsuki and Ren’s faces. It’s definitely not the same.
“So, how old are you two?”
He seems intent on keeping the conversation going.
“I’m 21 years old—and The Love Hunter!”
A “The Love Hunter”… What on earth is that? It’s hard to talk to Motoyasu-kun. He seems really dependable, though… Anyway, since Itsuki turned to look at me, I decided to introduce myself.
“I’m 20. I’m a college student.”
“I see. So, everyone… I’m just guessing here, but you were summoned to another world, right?”
“Yeah, but… when we came to, we weren’t in human form—for some reason, we were in this form.”
I raised one hand to show off my own appearance.
“Same here… On my way home from cram school—”

With that, Itsuki and Ren each told us how they’d ended up in this other world. One got hit by a truck on his way home from cram school, and the other saved his childhood friend from a random attacker on his way home from school—and got summoned to this other world… Is that a reincarnation? And… Motoyasu is sniffing me for some reason. What the hell are you doing? Give me a break with the attention.
“Motoyasu… what about Kitamura-kun?”
“Please just call me Motoyasu, okay?”
Man, I really, really don’t want to call him that. I do think he looks cute, though. He tries to call me ‘Father’ and sniffs me—what on earth are you, anyway?
“So, Motoyasu-san, how did you end up in this world?”
“Hmm…”
Why are you getting lost in thought right now? Did you forget? Motoyasu looks at me, Itsuki, and Ren while blinking rapidly.
“…I ended up in this world after a bunch of pigs who were stalking me without permission barged into my house, tried to force me into a double suicide, and stabbed me.”
“Pigs?”
“Pigs are pigs. They’re selfish creatures who throw tantrums when things don’t go their way and spread malicious rumors when they don’t get the response they want.”
Assuming Motoyasu is human… “pigs”—based on that explanation, he’s someone you can actually have a conversation with…
“If we assume he’s human, would that make him a woman?”
“Ah, I guess so? Harassed by a woman, dragged into a forced double suicide, killed, and then reincarnated as a rabbit in another world?”
“That’s right.”
“Your tone is quite odd, but you’re clearly no stranger to combat.”
“It’s a skill I honed long ago. My body reacts instinctively to any sense of danger.”

I’m thinking, ‘This isn’t some novel about being summoned to another world…’ but it really is exactly that kind of situation. I’ve read those kinds of stories, too. You know… the mysterious, battle-hardened protagonist who instantly senses that the person who summoned him doesn’t like him and is about to do something, so he slaughters everyone around him and makes a clean getaway. I mean, there’s no way anyone could have that kind of situational awareness, right? Well, in our case, we were suddenly yelled at to “Kill them!” so it’s not that strange that our bodies reacted. Even Inu… Ren was in a fighting stance right after Motoyasu.
“Ren was able to move too, wasn’t he?”
“It was a situation I’d already thought through to some extent in my mind.”
Is it only natural to be on guard? When I turn my face toward the Itsuki… tree, he raises both hands as if to say, “Come on, that’s taking it too far,” and responds with his body.
“What about you, Naofumi-san?”
“I was reading a book when I started to lose consciousness, and before I knew it, I’d been summoned.”

Come to think of it… I feel like I heard a voice right after I realized what was happening. It was just before the smoke started rising. It sounded familiar… but it happened so suddenly that I can’t quite remember it clearly. And that cloth… that was the outfit I was wearing, right?
“The book…”

“Ah, it was *The Book of the Four Holy Weapons*. It’s a story where the Sword Hero, Spear Hero, Bow Hero, and Shield Hero are summoned to a world in crisis called *Nami* to face its threats. The page describing the Shield Hero was blank.”
“Sword.”
“Bow…”
Ren and Itsuki are looking at the weapons they each hold in their hands.
“The situation does match, but did we really look like this?”
“Well… since it was a novel, the character designs weren’t very detailed… but I don’t think there was any mention of us being in animal form.”
“It’s a pretty strange situation. I have absolutely no idea how we ended up looking like this.”
“Yeah. It’s more like… rather than a video game, ‘reincarnation in another world’ is the more accurate description.”
Whether Ren and Itsuki agreed or not, they silently nodded.
“Reincarnated in another world as animals?”
“Those guys were talking about ‘Beastmen,’ weren’t they? Given our situation, it does make sense that we’d think we’ve been summoned as Beastmen.”
“So why would they suddenly try to kill us? Was there something inconvenient about that?”
“I don’t know. But since they said they couldn’t acknowledge us as heroes, doesn’t that mean we’re the heroes?”
That’s true… I can’t take this shield off, no matter how hard I try. It’s stuck to my body. And Motoyasu, the rabbit, is staying quiet here. Is he the type who thinks before he speaks?
“Well… it seems like there are stats, which is pretty typical for a game.”
“Huh? Really?”
“I noticed that too! Don’t you see an icon in the corner of your vision?”
Following his advice, I stared blankly into space, and at the edge of my vision, I saw a mark that stood out strangely.
“Try focusing your attention on it.”
There was a soft ‘ping’ sound, and just like a computer browser, a large icon appeared in my field of vision.
Naofumi Iwatani | Status: Peckul | Class: Shield Hero | Lv. 1 | Equipment: Small Shield (Legendary Weapons) | Skills: None | Magic: None
There are various entries just at a glance, but I’ll skip over them. It feels strangely like a video game.
“Under ‘Status,’ it says ‘Peckul’… what’s that?”
“Mine says ‘Inult.’”
“It’s Riska, right?”
“I’m Usaunny, hop!”
Don’t strike a pose right there, Rabbit Motoyasu—you’re definitely enjoying this situation, aren’t you?
“I don’t really get it, but I see that ‘Peckul’ is apparently a status, and there’s Lv. 1 and all sorts of other stuff.”
“Ah, maybe if we find a way to raise our level, we’ll get stronger?”
“That’s right. Though, this system… it looks familiar.”
“It’s dangerous to jump to conclusions. Even if it’s similar, we should keep an open mind.”
“…You’re right. Even if it were a game we knew, there’s no way we’d end up looking like this right off the bat and almost get killed.”
“That’s true. The weapon enhancement methods look familiar, though.”
“Um… this is it, right?”
When I asked everyone about the Help menu, they nodded in agreement. Then, everyone shared their insights.
“There aren’t many ways to upgrade Naofumi’s weapon.”
“I think the fragments can be used by everyone. My help file even includes options for Ren and Itsuki.”
“That would mean an astronomical number of upgrades.”
“So, Itsuki, you’re satisfied with just a few upgrades?”
Itsuki looked annoyed by Motoyasu the Rabbit’s provocation.
“No, I’m not. Fine, then. I’ll just believe that our weapons follow a common standard and can be used accordingly.”
“I truly believe that. Well, though I doubt it’ll actually work.”
“I’d appreciate it if you’d stop with that provocative tone. It’s unpleasant.”
Usagi Motoyasu laughed heartily, “HAHAHA.” He’s nice to me, but he’s so provocative toward Itsuki… I wonder if it’s some kind of rodent pride?
“Since it looks like there’s a party feature, I’ll go ahead and form a party.”

With a *pop*, Motoyasu the Rabbit fiddled with something, and a party invitation appeared on my status icon, so I accepted it. It’s just like forming a party in an online game. Then, Motoyasu the Rabbit gave his spear a light swing… and when he gripped it, I had the illusion that our figures had become somewhat translucent. Was it just my imagination?
“Anyway, shouldn’t we wrap up this break and get out of here?”
“…You’re right. We really need to get out of here as fast as possible right now.”
“Since we’re underground, why don’t we head out to the courtyard first and see if we can escape through the castle gates?”
“Is that difficult? Should we check?”
“Itsuki looks like a squirrel—he could probably climb the walls.”
“But even if I’m the only one who can do it, we still won’t be able to escape.”
“Well, you’re right. We’ll have to consider a head-on breakthrough as well.”
Hiding from the soldiers’ footsteps, we step out into the courtyard to check the castle gates.
“We absolutely cannot allow a Beastman to be summoned! Men! You must kill them all!”
A man who looked like a king was striding purposefully, leading his soldiers and taking control of the castle gate. Could that guy actually be the king?
“Security’s really tight. Breaking through there will be tough unless we go all out like in a *Musou* game.”
“Should we give it a shot?”

Shushu! Motoyasu the rabbit is showing some enthusiasm, but honestly, right after being summoned—at Level 1—it’s probably impossible for us. I mean, he might have enough initial Attack Power to impale us, but still.
“No… let’s hold off on that.”
“In classic games like this, castles usually have secret passages, right?”
If an event like this happened out of the blue, in a game, the story would usually lead to an escape route through a different choice.
“That’s true. It’s likely to be inside a well or underground… there’s a chance we could get out that way.”
“Then let’s head over there. I’m sure there’s an underground passage.”
So we decided to head back toward the underground once more.
So, we went underground, but… it turns out this was an underground prison, and there were prisoners locked up in cells. Maybe it’s a good thing, but none of them are looking our way.
“Somehow… they look like a race of Beastmen.”
Half of the prisoners had animal ears. Some even had features that made them look almost entirely like animals. Wow… Beastmen. I’m kind of the same right now, though. We’ve also shrunk a bit.
“We probably shouldn’t just go around trying to rescue them, right?”
“Yeah. We might get attacked out of the blue, and if we get caught up in a commotion, those guys will notice us.”

Holding our breath and searching for an escape route, we made our way through the underground prison… but before we knew it, Motoyasu the Rabbit had taken the lead. Soon… Motoyasu the Rabbit’s ears twitched as he spotted one of the cells. The semi-transparent aura around it vanished in an instant. Then Motoyasu the Rabbit peered into the cell.
“Hm? It’s been noisy for a while now… A Beastman? Were they brought here by the soldiers? It’s deplorable that the people of this country have even rounded up such small creatures.”
Inside the cell was… a beautiful woman—she looked like a female knight—hanging with her arms bound by chains. Itsuki looked back and forth between me and the woman who looked like a knight.
“She seems like someone we can talk to. Should we ask her some questions to get a handle on the situation?”
“Are you sure that’s a good idea?”
“She’s in a cell, and she seems sympathetic to us, so as long as we’re careful with our responses, we should be fine. After all, she doesn’t have a clue what’s going on right now.”
“I guess so… I don’t think it’d be a bad idea to talk to her. Here.”
“Please let me handle this, pyon!”
“I’m a little nervous about leaving it to Motoyasu. Naofumi-san, as the next-eldest here. Can I count on you?”
“Got it.”
So, I decided to step up as the spokesperson and ask the woman who looked like a knight.
“I’d prefer if you could just stay quiet for now, though. We were suddenly summoned from another world, nearly killed by the summoners, and barely managed to escape here.”
“What? What do you mean… Wait, you guys, those weapons you’re holding…”
“This?”

Just as I said that, Motoyasu—the rabbit—started rolling his spear back and forth, changing its shape. Oh, I saw that in the help section. It said that if you insert materials, the weapon unlocks and you can change its form. When did he even insert the materials?
“Those characteristics match the hero from legend… Could it be that the commotion earlier was caused by a Beastman being summoned as the hero!?”
“It seems you’ve figured out what’s going on.”
“Well… we just got here out of the blue and barely escaped with our lives. If you don’t mind, I’d like to ask you a few things. Why did those guys try to kill us?”

“Well… our country, Melromarc, is a human-supremacist nation that views Demi-Humans as enemies. In that context, the legendary hero—a Beastman—was summoned. And since the hero is revered for having saved the world, he’s become an object of worship.”
I see! So, in this country, humans are the embodiment of justice, and the Hero—who is an object of worship—appeared as a Beastman, a member of an enemy race.
“They’re probably trying to cover up the fact that a Beastman Hero was summoned…”
“That’s a plausible explanation.”
“They’ll be desperate to kill us.”
“But what should we do? Going in head-on is out of the question—the security is way too tight…”

“If I were to leave here and speak to the king… well, it’d be tough for a hero who’s a Beastman. This country is that harsh on Beastmen and Demi-Humans. I, too, am currently imprisoned for taking the law into my own hands against those who hunted down Demi-Humans as slaves in my father’s fiefdom—a place known for its friendship with Demi-Humans—which was devastated by the Wave.”
Wow… this person seems like a pretty decent person. If it’s true, I’d like to help him.
“The Wave…”
It’s the same disaster mentioned in the *Book of the Four Holy Weapons* I read.

“Ah, my father’s territory was devastated by the Wave. Presumably, a Hero will be summoned to save the world from this crisis. You two were summoned for that… but since our races are inconvenient for the country, we were almost killed on the spot.”
I see… So that’s why we’re being targeted and are barely managing to escape like this.
“It’s quite a twist of fate that the hero is a Beastman… I think it would be right to hand the hero over to another country, but the kingdom probably won’t allow it.”
“Um… my name is Naofumi. And you are?”
“…Eclair Seaetto.”
So, Ms. Eclair.
“I sense a draft over here. I’m sure there’s a secret escape route.”
“Well then…”
“No, wait… Could you take me with you? I’d like you to serve as my escort. I had intended to wait until the queen returned, but it seems I can’t afford to wait any longer.”
We all look at each other.
“What should we do? She seems to know the situation fairly well, and I don’t get the impression she’s guilty of anything serious.”

“From the looks of it, she seems to be human. If we get out of here, we won’t be able to get supplies in town, so if she’s willing to help us, it might be a good idea.” “The problem is the wanted poster and all that, but according to what we’ve heard, she’s a noblewoman—maybe she has some allies?”
“What should we do?”

Hmm… It’s one event after another, but I’m actually getting a little excited. It feels like it’s all been set up—as if someone who seems to be on our side and doing the right thing has been captured. She reminds me of the female knight from the sixth volume of *The Last Illusion*, so I feel like it might be okay to take her with us.
“There’s a chance she’ll betray us the moment we save her, though…”
“There’s no end to being suspicious. We’ve got no choice but to run anyway.”
“You’re right…”
“Well then, let’s go save her!”
With a sharp slash, Motoyasu cuts through the metal bars of the cell and frees Eclair.
“Thank you.”
“I think there’s an escape route ahead, so let’s go.”
“Yeah. I’ll bring up the rear.”

So, relying on Motoyasu’s keen hearing, we made our way through the underground tunnels and emerged into what looked like a waterway. There was a locked section along the way, but Motoyasu physically cut through it with his spear so we could pass.
“It seems they’ve noticed we escaped into the waterway.”
Motoyasu twitched his ears, having sensed it.
“Are we okay?”
“They’re still way behind us. We’ll make it out alive. Even if they catch up, we’ll just take them out. Don’t underestimate a hero, pyon.”
Thinking to myself, “Wow, we’re moving through this pretty easily,” we followed Motoyasu’s lead down the waterway.
“I think it’d be best if my Father carried us from here on, pyon.”
Then, at a spot where we could see a light and the current was getting a bit faster, Motoyasu made a suggestion.
“Ah, if Mr. Naofumi the penguin guides us, I think we can make it.”
“I don’t want to.”
For some reason, Ren refused right then and there.
“Why not? We’re almost out of here.”
“You guys get out there; I’m taking a different route.”
What on earth is going on? We were all set to go together just a moment ago—why the sudden change?
“You can’t swim, can you?! Hahahaha!”
Motoyasu clutched his stomach and laughed, pointing at Ren, who began to tremble uncontrollably.
“That’s not it! I can swim!”
“…It looks like he’s hit the nail on the head.”
“That’s why I’m saying I can swim! This is ridiculous.”
“But if we go back the way we came, we might run into the soldiers. I’ll carry you, so just stay still.”
“Whoa! Don’t pick me up! I can swim!”
“Lord Iwatani, can you take the lead?”
“Got it. Alright, everyone, let’s go.”
“Yeah.”
“Let’s go!”
And so, Itsuki and Motoyasu followed right behind me… but Itsuki’s cheeks puffed out like a swim ring.
“Whoa! What’s going on! My cheeks are puffing out on their own—”
“Ugh, seriously… I’ll carry you, so just stay still.”
“You’re making a pretty good life preserver.”

Eclair-san held Itsuki like a life preserver and carried Ren on her back. Ren… was perched on Eclair-san’s shoulder as if determined not to get wet. Just like that, we swam all the way through the waterway and made it out to the open air.
“I have no idea why my cheek pouches suddenly puffed up—this is a total mess.”
“How about that! I didn’t drown, did I?”
“Ren, I get that you don’t like water, so please be quiet. I’m the one in serious trouble here.”
“Never mind that—we’re out now. We need to make a quick getaway.”

After leaving the waterway, Eclair draped a ragged cloth she’d found along the way over herself, and we hid inside it as we made our way through the castle town, trying to avoid being noticed. It seemed soldiers were setting up a tight cordon around the castle. Furthermore… there were wanted posters up with sketches that looked just like us.

“These are the vicious Beastmen who infiltrated the castle. Report them the moment you spot them, and kill them no matter what! Don’t listen to a word these guys say! They’re vicious criminals who’ve killed dozens of people inside the castle.”

Motoyasu and Ren attacked them so fiercely they couldn’t move, but I doubt they actually killed them… I didn’t know what happened to the knight who let out that bloodcurdling scream, but it was still within the range where he could be treated. This is another world, so there must be healing magic, right?
“Eclair-san.”
“What is it?”
“Is there such a thing as healing magic?”
“Yes, there is.”
That’s a relief. Then that knight probably isn’t dead either.
“In any case, we’d better hurry out of the castle town—before the gates close.”
“You’re right, Eclair.”
“Got it. Everyone, hold on to me. Let’s hurry.”
“Let’s go!”
Then, as Motoyasu gripped his spear again, I felt as if we’d become semi-transparent. Just like that, we managed to make it out of the castle town.
“Now that we’re this far, I guess we can breathe a sigh of relief… maybe.”
“I hope so… but what should we do now?”

“Let’s go to someone I know. There’s a person there who shares the same ideals as my father, who has a deep understanding of Demi-Humans and Beastmen. If we can get their cooperation, that should work out. Right now, the castle guards are too busy investigating the castle town, so if we move while they’re occupied, we shouldn’t have any trouble.”
“You’re right. Then, please lead the way.”
And so, guided by Ms. Eclair, we set off.

The sun was setting… and since we were completely penniless, we decided to avoid attention and spend the night outdoors… We chatted with everyone around the campfire. Dinner? Since everyone had helped defeat the monsters we’d encountered, I cooked the meal, and we all ate together. I’d managed to get my hands on a knife while we were fleeing, so I was glad I could use it. Though, when I thought I could fight with this knife and tried to grip it, it bounced right off my hand—turns out I can only use it as a shield.
“Phew… These skewers tasted better than I expected.”
“It was great that we could use the medicinal herbs we found along the way as seasoning.”
“Naofumi, you’re a great cook.”
“It’s not that great.”

Sitting in front of the crackling campfire, I feel a bit excited—even if it’s a bit inappropriate. My heart was in my throat at first… but when I think about being in another world on an adventure, it feels like a dream.
“I’m going to the bathroom for a bit.”
“Ah, Motoyasu-san, are you going for another meal? Make sure to freshen up your breath, okay?”
Itsuki made a remark to Motoyasu that bordered on provocation.
“HAHAHA, I’m not eating, you know? Well then, I’ll be off.”
With that, Motoyasu rustled off. He didn’t come back for quite a while.
“Motoyasu, I wonder what on earth he’s doing?”
“I’m back. I took the opportunity to scout the area.”
“Oh… is that so? Any signs of soldiers?”
“None at all.”

That’s the most important thing. By the way, as for what he was actually doing later on… well, it seems this guy—the root of all our troubles—had gone to rescue the girl. He’ll be introduced later. In any case, exhausted as we were, we took turns resting as our life on the run continued. We hitched a ride on a shared horse-drawn carriage in a village along the way. It was my first time riding in a covered wagon. It looks like our life on the run will continue for a while yet… but somehow we ended up agreeing that we should head for either the country of Faubrey or the country of Siltvelt. According to Ms. Eclair, heading to Faubrey would be best, but since escaping from Melromarc is the priority for now… our journey continues. And so, together with my reliable companions, the curtain rose on an adventure that, while terrible, also looked like it would be fun.
To be continued... (not really).
